question: Zinc + Sulphuric acid → Zinc sulphate + ______
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Zinc + Sulphuric acid → Zinc sulfate + Hydrogen**

 
 
• The reactants are zinc and sulphuric acid, whereas, the products are zinc sulfate and hydrogen.
 
• In the given molecular reaction, (g) indicates gas i.e. hydrogen is a gas.
 
• This is a double replacement reaction where does Zn up replaces the H in the sulfuric acid.
